newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds up on back of German data, comments.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds up on back of German data, comments.

text.p: Irish government bonds were up in thin late trade on Thursday on the back of stronger than expected German economic data and bearish comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, dealers said.

"We saw a reasonable enough performance from the Irish market on the day. Overall, markets were quiet. Markets did respond favourably to the German data and comments this morning but they have been trading in tight ranges since then," one dealer said.
Dealers said there had been good domestic and overseas interest in the short-end and the five-year bond was the best performer on the day.
The Bundesbank reported M3 money, one of its key policy indicators, grew at an 11.7 percent rate as compared with the fourth quarter 1996 average rate.
Dealers said this exceeded the bank's self-set 3.5 to 6.5 percent growth corridor and appeared to reduce the chances for another rate cut.

But more importantly, dealers said comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer that a decline in Germany's interest rates would be unlikely in the short-term poured cold water on hopes for another easing.
The Bundesbank kept its three leading interest rates unchanged at its policy-setting council meeting today as expected by the market.

By 1635 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 33 pence from Wednesday's close at 103.28 to yield 5.66 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 13 pence from the close at 111.28 to yield 6.37 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 135 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 89 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.
Looking ahead, market focus is likely to remain on exchange rates, dealers said.
"The exchange rates are driving the market. Between sterling and the dollar being quite volatile, we have plenty to keep an eye on," the dealer said.
